articles.title: Python's pre-declared constants are kinda weird
articles.summary: Python's pre-declared constants are a peculiar feature that can lead to unexpected behavior when used in certain situations. These constants, including True, False, None, __debug__, Ellipsis, and NotImplemented, have different behaviors depending on the context in which they are used. This can result in errors such as SyntaxErrors when attempting to assign or delete these constants. The constants are not identifiers in the classical sense, but rather lexical tokens that are resolved during regular name resolution, not in the lexer itself.

Root LPEs are also coming out faster than Google can ship patches, allowing for C2PA forgeries without requiring hardware attacks.

The bug is likely due to a misunderstanding of the EPOLLIN event's behavior on 32-bit ARM and i386 systems.
